laws.rule: Foreign visitors entering Quintana Roo (which includes Cancún, Playa del Carmen, Tulum, Cozumel and Isla Mujeres) must pay a state fee for foreign visitors, known as Visitax: 2.5 UMA, about MXN 293.27 (about A$22.16) from 1 February 2026 (Ley de Derechos, art. 51-Octies). It's paid online through the state's Visitax portal or companies authorised by the state tax service (SATQ), which issue a QR-code receipt. Foreign visitors who enter through the state's southern border are exempt.
The state's Visitax portal says the fee is mandatory for all foreign tourists, children and infants included, whatever their departure route, Cozumel included.

Cruise passengers whose ship calls at a Quintana Roo port pay a state fee of US$5 (about A$7.10), charged by the cruise line when the fare is bought and only once per voyage; proof of that payment exempts them from Visitax (art. 51-Nonies).

At several archaeological zones the state charges its own fee for using the state service units next to the site (art. 51-Bis). For foreign visitors it's 4.25 UMA, about MXN 498.57 (about A$37.68), at Tulum, Cobá, Xel-Há, Muyil, Kohunlich, Ichkabal, Xcaret, San Miguelito, San Gervasio (Cozumel) and the Museo Maya de Cancún, and 2 UMA, about MXN 234.62 (about A$17.73), at El Rey, El Meco, Chacchoben, Dzibanché-Kinichná and Oxtankah. Some groups pay half (people over 60 or under 10, students and teachers, people with disability); Mexican residents are exempt on Sundays.

Isla Mujeres municipality charges an environmental sanitation fee (Derecho de Saneamiento Ambiental) of 30% of the daily UMA, about MXN 35.19 (about A$2.66): per visitor per night for anyone staying in a hotel, hostel, guest house or other lodging (collected by the lodging), and once per visitor for those who don't stay overnight (collected by the passenger ferry operator, or with the port fee for private and tour boats). Visitors using the boats of local Isla Mujeres cooperatives, and people working in the municipality, are exempt (Ley de Hacienda del Municipio de Isla Mujeres, art. 54 to 58).

Cozumel municipality charges an environmental sanitation fee on everyone over two arriving by air or sea: 15% of the daily UMA per person, about MXN 17.60 (about A$1.33), for stays under 24 hours (collected with the ferry ticket, or the port fee for private boats), and 30% of the daily UMA per room per night, about MXN 35.19 (about A$2.66), for longer stays (collected by the accommodation). Someone who paid the day rate and then stays is exempt for the first night. Residents and people working there are exempt (Ley de Hacienda del Municipio de Cozumel, art. 135 Bis to 135 Septies).

Quintana Roo charges a state lodging tax (impuesto al hospedaje) on paid stays in hotels, motels, inns, camping and caravan areas, timeshare and tourist marinas, and on stays offered by hosts, including through digital platforms. The rate is 5% of the invoiced or contracted price, or 6% where the host or the booking platform collects the payment (Ley del Impuesto al Hospedaje, art. 4 and 8). The provider collects it from the guest; the state finance secretariat administers it.

In Arrecifes de Cozumel National Park, CONANP's visitor rules say: keep at least 1.5 m from the reefs; don't feed or disturb wildlife; don't touch the reef; don't anchor; don't fish; don't use gloves, knives or rods; don't use sunscreen; and hire boats and guides authorised by CONANP.

In Sian Ka'an Biosphere Reserve, CONANP's visitor rules say: no sunscreen; no campfires; don't take plants or animals; don't mark trees or archaeological monuments; don't leave rubbish; no fishing; stay on authorised trails; no pets; and no sound equipment.
In Isla Contoy National Park, CONANP's visitor rules say: no smoking; touch nothing; no sunscreen; and a life jacket is compulsory for snorkelling. Marked trails are walked with a guide.

In Costa Occidental de Isla Mujeres, Punta Cancun y Punta Nizuc National Park, the visible visitor rules include: a life jacket is compulsory; touch no species; don't feed fish; hire authorised service providers; and don't anchor on seagrass. The page hides the full list behind a link.

Tulum National Park: CONANP's visitor rules say respect signs and ranger instructions and walk only on established trails; don't take plants or animals; don't use sound equipment that disturbs wildlife; no pets; no heavy vehicles; and beach access is until 19:00.

local-law.notes: Amounts use the 2026 UMA (Unidad de Medida y Actualización, a federal reference unit: MXN 117.31 a day from 1 February 2026, INEGI) and A$1 = about MXN 13.23 (RBA 30 October 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040; Banco de México FIX for 30 October 2026, USD 1 = MXN 18.7962). Other Quintana Roo municipalities set their own sanitation fees; those aren't checked here. Reef and protected-area rules in this state are mostly federal (CONANP) and aren't recorded at state level.

layers.process: Entry fee of MXN 225 per person per day (about A$17.01; A$1 = about MXN 13.23 (RBA 30 October 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040; Banco de Mexico FIX, USD 1 = MXN 18.7962)). Exempt: older adults, pensioners and retirees, people with disability and children under 12 (credential shown on entry). 75% off for students and teachers with a credential; 50% off for Mexican nationals and foreign residents who show an official document. Open 6:00 to 22:00 (6:00 to 23:00 in summer). Visitors must hire boats and guides authorised by CONANP.
